flashcard_questions.q: What is a cool down in sport?
flashcard_questions.a: A series of exercises after activity that returns the body to its resting state.

flashcard_questions.q: How long should a cool down last?
When does DOMS usually develop after exercise?
What actually causes the soreness of DOMS?
flashcard_questions.a: Tiny tears in the muscle fibres.

flashcard_questions.q: Which waste product does a cool down help clear from the muscles?
Which muscles should cool down stretches target?
flashcard_questions.a: The major muscle groups used during the activity.

flashcard_questions.q: What is blood pooling after exercise?
flashcard_questions.a: Blood collecting in the veins of the legs instead of circulating.

flashcard_questions.q: Which stage of a cool down prevents blood pooling?
Which type of stretching belongs in a cool down?
Why is stretching more effective in a cool down than in a warm up?
flashcard_questions.a: The muscles are still warm, so they stretch further.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the purpose of deep breathing at the end of a cool down?
flashcard_questions.a: To relax the body and calm the nervous system.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a cool down help muscle tissue repair?
flashcard_questions.a: It maintains blood flow, delivering oxygen and nutrients to the muscles.

flashcard_questions.q: Which hormone do controlled breathing and gentle movement lower?
Which psychological benefit does a team gain from cooling down together?

notes: 15 cards: 5 term-to-definition, 3 value cards (5-10 min, 24-72 h), 4 cause-and-effect, 3 stage/label. Kept the DOMS-is-not-lactic-acid split across two cards because the lesson flags it as the common error.
